title: How Long Does Interior Painting Take? Realistic Timelines
description: Most single rooms take 1–2 days and whole-home wall repaints take about 2–4 days. Here's what drives the timeline, how scheduling works, and how to keep your project moving.
author: Chris Petkau
content:
Short answer: with a professional crew, most single rooms like a bedroom, living room or dining room take one to two days. A whole-home wall repaint usually takes two to four days. Adding ceilings, trim, doors, cabinets, big color changes or drywall repair adds time, and so does the drying time between coats.

Typical Interior Painting Timelines

  • One standard room (walls only): about 1 day

  • One room with ceiling, trim and doors: about 1–2 days

  • Whole-home walls: about 2–4 days, depending on square footage, color changes and patching

  • Whole-home walls, ceilings, trim and doors: longer; your estimate should include a timeline for your specific scope

These figures assume a professional crew. A DIY room often takes a full weekend or more once you count moving furniture, prep, two coats and cleanup.

What Makes a Project Take Longer

  • Prep and repairs. Patching nail holes, fixing drywall damage, caulking trim and sanding glossy surfaces all come before the first coat. This is time well spent: it's what makes the finish last. See our interior preparation process.

  • Big color changes. Going from dark to light, or covering a bold accent wall, can mean a primer coat plus two finish coats.

  • Trim, doors and cabinets. Enamel work is slower and needs longer drying between coats than wall paint.

  • High ceilings and two-story foyers. These need taller ladders, scaffolding and more setup.

  • How many colors you choose. Every extra color means more cut lines and more switching between colors.

  • Furniture and access. Rooms that are cleared ahead of time start faster.

  • Humidity. Gulf Coast humidity can stretch drying time between coats, especially in rooms without good airflow.

How Scheduling Works Before Day One

The time on site is only part of the picture. With us, scope and colors are usually settled two to three weeks ahead. Materials are ordered and colors and sheens confirmed about a week before the start date. Once work begins, we stay until it's complete. You can see the full sequence on our what to expect page.

How to Keep Your Project on Schedule

  • Pick your colors and sheens before the start date, and sample them on your walls first

  • Clear small items, wall art and breakables from the rooms being painted

  • Mention any repairs you know about at the estimate so they're in the plan

  • Group rooms so the crew can work through the house without backtracking

Frequently Asked Questions

How long does it take to paint a bedroom?

A standard bedroom usually takes one to two days, depending on size, ceiling height and how much patching the walls need.

Can I stay in my house while the interior is painted?

Yes, most homeowners do. Low-odor paints and painting one area at a time keep the house livable.

How long should paint dry before I move furniture back?

Walls are usually dry to the touch within hours, but paint keeps curing for weeks. Wait at least a day before pushing furniture against walls, and be gentle with fresh trim and doors.
